title: Transcriptional Plasticity and Platform-Specific Immune Targetability in IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma
content: IDH-wildtype glioblastoma contains coexisting developmental and injury-associated malignant cell states whose proportions are shaped by genotype, microenvironment and treatment. This plasticity influences immune targetability, but the relevant biological gates differ across therapeutic platforms. Mutation-directed vaccines and T-cell receptor therapies require sufficient cancer-cell coverage, mutant-allele expression, peptide processing, HLA presentation and functional T-cell access. Chimeric antigen receptor T cells bypass peptide-HLA recognition but depend on surface-antigen density, spatial coverage, normal-tissue selectivity, tumor-cell adhesion and effector persistence. Oncolytic viruses additionally require entry-receptor expression, tumor permissiveness, local spread and productive innate activation before endogenous antigen release can contribute to adaptive immunity. Transcription-factor and chromatin circuits can alter several of these gates by regulating lineage programs, interferon responses, chemokines and myeloid interactions. We integrate single-cell and epigenomic models of glioblastoma state with clinical evidence from personalized vaccines, dendritic-cell vaccines, immune-checkpoint blockade, CAR-T cells and oncolytic viruses. Early-phase studies demonstrate immunogenicity and occasional marked regressions, whereas randomized anti-PD-1 trials have been negative and antigen loss or state adaptation remains frequent. We therefore propose a platform-specific, state-aware workflow that separates target architecture from barrier diagnosis, combines multiregion DNA and RNA profiling with spatial protein validation and, where feasible, immunopeptidomics, and links combination therapy to a measured failure mode. Prospective trials should include longitudinal blood, cerebrospinal-fluid and tissue pharmacodynamics and should distinguish target engagement from comparative clinical benefit.
